subject: Private deployment evidence: escrow-tiering + short-term audit access proposal
messages:
From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@luminahealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy evidence & operator access ask

Sofia — thanks for the demo last week. We’re lining up procurement and legal on a private VPC deployment and have two asks we need to lock into the MSA / Order Form before internal approval: 

1) Evidence deposit / escrow-like mechanism: our security team wants a documented pathway to verify that the runtime image + operator runbook can be accessed in a controlled way if Redwood ceases to operate in region. We don’t require source code; we want validated snapshots and a handover plan.

2) Temporary audit access: for the pilot we’ll need a short audit window (read-only console + logs) to validate the snapshot and procedures.

Can you send an approach your legal team is comfortable with for including this in the MSA + an estimate of timeline? I attached the NDA we use in case it helps.

Thanks,
Amir
Director, IT Security — Lumina Health
attachments: NDA_Lumina.pdf

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: Amir Patel <amir.patel@luminahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy evidence & operator access ask

Amir — appreciate the clarity. High level proposal we can work into an MSA addendum: 

- Escrow-lite (staged evidence split): Redwood deposits a time-stamped, checksummed runtime snapshot and operational runbook to a mutually agreed secure escrow custodian. The deposit is verification-only (not source code) and is refreshed on major releases or every 6 months, whichever is sooner.

- Witnessless verification path: instead of an in-person witness, we provide cryptographic attestations + a downloadable forensic snapshot for your audit team to validate in a controlled environment.

- Temporary audit console: a read-only, timeboxable console credential set (30-day window by default) scoped to verify snapshot integrity and KV-rotation/response procedure. Access is logged and limited to named auditors.

Next steps: I’m looping DAVID (legal) for specific addendum language and MARISSA for operational runbook sequencing. I’ve also attached a short PDF with the proposed flow. If this meets your bar in principle, suggest a short call next week to run the redlines.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference
attachments: escrow-lite-proposal.pdf

Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Draft language for MSA addendum (evidence & audit access)

Amir / Sofia — looping in legal input. Below is a concise set of redline points we plan to propose; I’ve attached a DOCX with tracked changes for the MSA addendum. Please review and identify any must-haves we missed.

Key proposed clauses (summary):
- "Escrowed Artifacts": define "Artifacts" as (i) checksummed runtime image artifacts, (ii) operator runbook and runbook checklist, (iii) configuration manifests necessary to instantiate the runtime. No source code, training data, or model weights beyond runtime binary are included.
- "Deposit Frequency": Redwood will deposit a new Artifact on major runtime releases or quarterly, whichever occurs first.
- "Release Trigger": Custodian will release Artifacts to Customer only upon a defined triggering event (Redwood insolvency, material MSA breach failing cure within 60 days, or written governmental order).
- "Temporary Audit Provision": Redwood will provision read-only audit credentials within 10 business days of a formal request for a timeboxed window (default 30 days), scoped to named auditors and subject to an NDA.
- "Liability/Security": cap on liability tied to Order Form; customer retains obligation to validate artifacts in their environment; Redwood maintains responsibility for secure deposit and attestations.

Open asks from our side: preferred custodian (we can propose two partners), acceptable deposit cadence (quarterly vs. 6 months), any special retention/regulatory constraints from Lumina (HIPAA data residency notes).

Attachments: MSA_Addendum_proposal.docx

I recommend a redline exchange via DocuSign for the Order Form addendum once we align the bullets above. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk legal through the proposed triggers.

Regards,
David Kim
Sr. Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Amir Patel <amir.patel@luminahealth.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: Sally O'Neill <sally.oneill@luminahealth.com>, procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft language for MSA addendum (evidence & audit access)

David / Sofia — thanks for the clear draft. A few quick notes from Lumina legal/security: 

1) Deposit cadence: quarterly would be preferred (we need up-to-date artifacts for our internal change control).
2) Release Trigger: add "material regulatory prohibition" as an additional trigger (e.g., if a regulator prohibits Redwood from operating in the region).
3) Temporary Audit Provision: we need an explicit rollback trigger example in the addendum (e.g., customer validation finds a configuration mismatch preventing safe operation). In that case, we propose a 14-day remediation/cure window with escrowed artifacts available for validation if unresolved.

I attached our markup with inline comments — page-level callouts on the Release Trigger wording and a proposed sentence for the rollback example. Also, please confirm the custodian options; if Redwood has a preferred partner, share the SOW so our procurement can review.

Amir
attachments: redlines_Lumina.markup.pdf
